sense: the doer, with a passive verb

terms.grammar: preposition with the ablative, after a passive verb; ā before consonants, ab before vowels and h
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.5.8: tē ā mē frāternē amārī
terms.comment: Only for a person, or a creature thought of as acting: ā cane … tenētur aper. A thing or a force that does it stands in the plain ablative, without ā (see “by”, the means): vīpera necat morsū.

terms.gloss: by (the person who has to do something)
terms.grammar: construction: the person in the dative, with the gerundive
evidence: Caes. BG 2.20.1: Caesarī omnia ūnō tempore erant agenda
terms.comment: With the gerundive Latin names the doer in the dative, not with ā: mihi eundum est, I have to go.

phrases.latin: cūrā ut valeās et nōs amēs et tibi persuādeās tē ā mē frāternē amārī
phrases.english: take care of yourself, love us, and be sure that you are loved by me like a brother

phrases.latin: jam trīstis nucibus puer relictīs clāmōsō revocātur ā magistrō
phrases.english: now the boy sadly leaves his nuts and is called back by the shouting schoolmaster

phrases.latin: parva necat morsū spatiōsum vīpera taurum: ā cane nōn magnō saepe tenētur aper
phrases.english: a small viper kills a huge bull with its bite; a boar is often held by a dog of no great size

phrases.latin: quōcumque diēī tempore inclāmātus ā puerō, quamvīs occultus atque abditus, ex īmō advolābat
phrases.english: at whatever time of day he was called by the boy, however hidden and out of sight, he came flying up from the depths

phrases.latin: Caesarī omnia ūnō tempore erant agenda
phrases.english: Caesar had everything to do at once
